```{r scan-global-adj, eval=imaging_ok && nrow(scan_all)>0}
if (nrow(scan_global_adj)) {
  cmp_glob <- inner_join(
    scan_all        %>% select(Tissue, token, Region, B_tiv = Beta, P_tiv = P),
    scan_global_adj %>% select(Tissue, token, B_glob = Beta, P_glob = P),
    by = c("Tissue", "token")) %>% arrange(P_tiv)
  cat(sprintf("Nominal hits before vs after adjusting for the tissue total: %d -> %d.\n",
              sum(cmp_glob$P_tiv < .05), sum(cmp_glob$P_glob < .05)))
  cmp_glob %>% head(12) %>%
    transmute(Tissue, Region,
              `TIV only` = sprintf("%.2f (p=%.3f)", B_tiv, P_tiv),
              `+ tissue total` = sprintf("%.2f (p=%.3f)", B_glob, P_glob),
              Verdict = ifelse(P_tiv < .05 & P_glob >= .05, "global shift",
                        ifelse(P_glob < .05, "regional", "ns"))) %>%
    kable(caption = paste("Regional effects before and after adjusting for the",
      "tissue compartment total. 'Global shift' means the region only looked",
      "different because the whole compartment did.")) %>%
    kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, bootstrap_options = c("striped","condensed"),
                  font_size = 11)
}
```

```{r scan-volcano, fig.width=9, fig.height=4.5, eval=imaging_ok && nrow(scan_all)>0}
vp <- scan_all %>% mutate(sig = ifelse(Q < .05, "FDR q<0.05",
                               ifelse(P < .05, "nominal p<0.05", "ns")))
ggplot(vp, aes(Beta, -log10(P), colour = sig)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(.05), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey70") +
  geom_point(alpha = .85, size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~ Tissue) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("FDR q<0.05" = "#D55E00",
                                 "nominal p<0.05" = "#000000", "ns" = "grey65")) +
  labs(title = "Whole-atlas scan: regional volume vs SAA status",
       subtitle = "Exploratory. Interpret against the detectable-effect bar reported above.",
       x = "β (SAA+ vs SAA−, SD units)", y = expression(-log[10](p)), colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r scan-by-system, fig.width=8, fig.height=4.5, eval=imaging_ok && nrow(scan_gm)>0}
## Is any anatomical system shifted as a whole? A one-sample test of the
## regional betas within each system — coherence, not significance-counting.
sys_shift <- scan_gm %>% group_by(System) %>%
  filter(n() >= 3) %>%
  summarise(k = n(), mean_beta = mean(Beta, na.rm = TRUE),
            p_shift = tryCatch(t.test(Beta)$p.value, error = function(e) NA_real_),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(mean_beta)

ggplot(sys_shift, aes(mean_beta, reorder(System, mean_beta),
                      fill = p_shift < .05)) +
  geom_col(width = .65) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey40") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "grey70", "TRUE" = "#D55E00"), guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "Mean regional effect by anatomical system (grey matter)",
       subtitle = "Average beta across the regions of each system; orange = p<0.05",
       x = "Mean β (SAA+ vs SAA−, SD units)", y = "")
kable(sys_shift %>% transmute(System, regions = k, mean_beta = round(mean_beta, 3),
                              p = round(p_shift, 4)),
      caption = paste("System-level coherence of the regional effects. These are",
        "eight pre-defined anatomical systems, not a scan, so raw p is reported",
        "without multiplicity adjustment.")) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, bootstrap_options = c("striped","condensed"))
```

## Left–right asymmetry

```{r asymmetry, eval=imaging_ok}
## Asymmetry index = (L − R) / ((L + R)/2). Signed, so a group difference means
## the pathology is lateralised differently, not just larger.
cat(sprintf("Asymmetry columns available in the imaging sample: %d of %d nigrostriatal regions.\n",
            sum(paste0("ai_", NIGRO) %in% names(img)), length(NIGRO)))

asym_res <- map_dfr(NIGRO, function(r) {
  cc <- paste0("ai_", r)
  if (!cc %in% names(img)) return(NULL)
  d <- img %>% mutate(AI = .data[[cc]], absAI = abs(.data[[cc]]))
  o1 <- fit_one("AI",    d, covars = setdiff(BASE_COVARS, "MRI_TIV"), zscore = FALSE)
  o2 <- fit_one("absAI", d, covars = setdiff(BASE_COVARS, "MRI_TIV"), zscore = FALSE)
  if (is.null(o1)) return(NULL)
  tibble(Region = pretty_region(r), n = o1$n, n_pos = o1$n_pos,
         Beta_signed = round(o1$Beta, 4), p_signed = round(o1$P, 4),
         Beta_abs = if (is.null(o2)) NA_real_ else round(o2$Beta, 4),
         p_abs    = if (is.null(o2)) NA_real_ else round(o2$P, 4))
})
if (nrow(asym_res)) {
  asym_res <- asym_res %>% mutate(q_signed = round(p.adjust(p_signed, "BH"), 3))
  kable(asym_res, caption = paste("Asymmetry of the nigrostriatal family.",
    "Signed = direction of lateralisation (L-R); abs = degree of lateralisation",
    "regardless of side.")) %>%
    kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, bootstrap_options = c("striped","condensed"))
  write.csv(asym_res, file.path(results_path, "Imaging_asymmetry.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
} else cat("No nigrostriatal asymmetry index could be modelled.")
```

## Sensitivity analyses

```{r sensitivity, eval=imaging_ok}
## (a) proportional normalisation instead of TIV as a covariate
## (b) IQR added as a covariate
## (c) restricted to scans within one year of sampling
prop_dat <- img
for (r in NIGRO) {
  cc <- paste0("gm_", r)
  if (cc %in% names(prop_dat) && "MRI_TIV" %in% names(prop_dat))
    prop_dat[[paste0("prop_", r)]] <- prop_dat[[cc]] / prop_dat$MRI_TIV
}
iqr_dat  <- img
near_dat <- img %>% filter(is.na(mri_gap) | mri_gap <= 365)

sens <- map_dfr(NIGRO, function(r) {
  base <- fit_one(paste0("gm_", r), img)
  pre  <- if (exists("img_raw") && (isTRUE(combat_ok) || isTRUE(restrict_ok)))
            fit_one(paste0("gm_", r), img_raw) else NULL
  prop <- if (paste0("prop_", r) %in% names(prop_dat))
    fit_one(paste0("prop_", r), prop_dat,
            covars = setdiff(BASE_COVARS, "MRI_TIV")) else NULL
  iqrm <- fit_one(paste0("gm_", r), iqr_dat,
                  covars = c(BASE_COVARS, "MRI_IQR_pct"))
  near <- fit_one(paste0("gm_", r), near_dat)
  if (is.null(base)) return(NULL)
  tibble(Region = pretty_region(r),
         `All protocols` = if (is.null(pre)) "—" else sprintf("%.2f (p=%.3f)", pre$Beta, pre$P),
         `TIV covariate` = sprintf("%.2f (p=%.3f)", base$Beta, base$P),
         `Proportional`  = if (is.null(prop)) "—" else sprintf("%.2f (p=%.3f)", prop$Beta, prop$P),
         `+ IQR`         = if (is.null(iqrm)) "—" else sprintf("%.2f (p=%.3f)", iqrm$Beta, iqrm$P),
         `MRI ≤1 y (n=%d)` = if (is.null(near)) "—" else sprintf("%.2f (p=%.3f)", near$Beta, near$P))
})
if (nrow(sens)) {
  names(sens)[ncol(sens)] <- sprintf("MRI <=1 y (n=%d)", nrow(near_dat))
  kable(sens, caption = paste("Nigrostriatal family across harmonisation,",
        "normalisation and inclusion choices. Beta in SD units except the",
        "proportional column. A large gap between the all-protocols column and",
        "the main estimate means scanner effects were doing real work.")) %>%
    kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, bootstrap_options = c("striped","condensed"))
}
```

```{r closing, results='asis', eval=imaging_ok}
cat(sprintf("
**Sample.** %d scans, %d SAA-positive. Detects |beta| >= %.2f SD at 80%% power;
smaller effects are out of reach, so nulls here are uninformative rather than
negative.

**Primary family.** %s

**Whole atlas.** %d grey-matter and %d white-matter regions; %d and %d survive
FDR. %s Roughly %d nominal hits are expected by chance in grey matter alone, so
single regions there are candidates, not results. The system-level plot is the
more reliable view: a real effect shifts a whole system, not one parcel.

**Harmonisation.** %s

**Excluded.** Ventricles and corpus callosum from the grey-matter analysis (their
Hammers grey-matter volume is partial-volume noise); ventricles from white matter.
",
nrow(img), n1, mde,
if (nrow(prim)) sprintf("Best region %s, beta = %.2f [%.2f, %.2f], p = %.3f, q = %.3f.",

  else if (isTRUE(combat_ok)) sprintf("ComBat over %d protocols, protecting the SAA contrast, sex, age and TIV.", n_batch)
  else if (isTRUE(covar_ok)) sprintf("Protocol carried as a covariate (smallest n = %d).", min_batch_n)
  else if (isTRUE(restrict_ok)) sprintf("Restricted to protocol %s; %d scan(s) excluded.", dominant, sum(batch_tab) - sum(batch_tab[dominant, ]))
  else "Not harmonised - state as a limitation."))
```


# Summary of methodological choices

```{r summary-notes, results='asis'}
cat(sprintf("
- **Merge.** Clinical visits paired with the biofluid sample closest in time (`visit_date`, not the baseline date). %s
- **Long-format REDCap.** Subject-level fields carried down within NHC before collapsing to one row per subject, so core symptoms and visit scores coexist.
- **Reading.** `guess_max = Inf`, without which readxl types the visit-level columns from the empty enrolment rows and discards their data.
- **SAA recoding.** Anchored patterns; every raw level is printed above for verification. Indeterminate results excluded (n = %d), not folded into either group.
- **Combined cohort.** Own-site result preferred, Munich as fallback — discordant pairs are no longer silently coded Positive. This cohort contains the Sant Pau cohort, so the two tables are not independent.
- **Plausibility limits.** Values outside each scale range are set to NA and counted. In this dataset the guard finds nothing: the impossible Mayo values seen previously (mean 21, SD 62 on a 0–4 scale) came from the baseline-date row selection picking the wrong rows, and the date fix alone resolves them. The guard remains as a regression check.
- **Tests.** Rank-based for continuous variables, Fisher for categorical, with SMD alongside the mean/risk difference and BH-FDR across each biomarker panel.
- **Coverage gate.** Assays with fewer than %d observations per group are omitted rather than printed as `NA (NA)`.
- **Imaging.** Both segmentations on the same subjects, volumes z-scored so structures of different size share an axis, with an a priori 3-structure family alongside the 7-structure FDR.
", merge_note, n_indet, MIN_PER_GROUP))
```

# References

Found with Undermind and read against the results above. The note on each line
is what it says about our finding, not a summary of the paper.

**Clinical features**

1. Coughlin DG, MacLeod KR, Middleton JS, et al. *Association of CSF
   alpha-Synuclein Seeding Amplification Assay Results With Clinical Features of
   Possible and Probable Dementia With Lewy Bodies.* Neurology 2024;103(3):e209656.
   doi:10.1212/WNL.0000000000209656
   — n = 191 DLB. RBD in 86% of SAA+ vs 62% of SAA- (p < 0.0001, OR 3.63):
   our RBD result replicates with a smaller effect. Hallucinations 50% vs 47%
   (p = 0.73): our null replicates theirs. MDS-UPDRS III 33.8 vs 25.6
   (p = 0.001): **we do not replicate this** — our UPDRS III and parkinsonism
   prevalence are flat. DaT-SPECT was not analysed against SAA status, so our
   DaT result has no direct published comparator.

**Glial markers and AD co-pathology**

2. Morenas-Rodriguez E, Alcolea D, Suarez-Calvet M, et al. *Different pattern of
   CSF glial markers between dementia with Lewy bodies and Alzheimer's disease.*
   Sci Rep 2019;9:7803. doi:10.1038/s41598-019-44173-8
   — YKL-40 elevation in DLB tracked tau, not synuclein, and was unrelated to
   amyloid status. GFAP was not measured. Sets the prior that glial markers in
   DLB follow AD co-pathology.

3. Cousins KAQ, Shaw LM, Chen-Plotkin A, et al. *Plasma GFAP associates with
   secondary Alzheimer's pathology in Lewy body disease.* Ann Clin Transl Neurol
   2022;9(6):802-813. doi:10.1002/acn3.51768
   — Plasma GFAP in Lewy body disease tracks concomitant amyloid. Our CSF GFAP
   elevation in SAA+ is amyloid-independent in both strata, i.e. against this
   account — but at n = 11 vs 11.

4. Honig LS, Kang MS, Lamoureux J, Marder K. *Cerebrospinal fluid seed
   aggregation assay and Alzheimer biomarkers in a Dementia with Lewy Body
   cohort.* Alzheimers Dement 2025;21(Suppl 2):e107531. doi:10.1002/alz70856_107531
   — No difference in amyloid or tau biomarker status between SAA+ and SAA-, and
   no evidence of increased AD pathology in SAA-. Our null a-path replicates
   this, which is why the mediation question resolves as "not amyloid-mediated".

**Imaging**

5. Tosun D, Landau SM, Weiner MW, Blauwendraat C; ADNI. *Neuroimaging features of
   CSF alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay positivity in elderly individuals
   in AD continuum.* Alzheimers Dement 2024;20(Suppl 2):e092637.
   doi:10.1002/alz.092637
   — Cortical atrophy differences by SAA status, but **no medial temporal or
   hippocampal effect**, and no subcortical analysis. Supports treating our
   medial-temporal volumetric signal as noise.

6. Cohen JS, Phillips JS, Das SR, et al. *Posterior hippocampal sparing in Lewy
   body disorders with Alzheimer's copathology: an in vivo MRI study.*
   Neuroimage Clin 2024;43:103714. doi:10.1016/j.nicl.2024.103714
   — Hippocampal involvement in Lewy body disease is driven by AD co-pathology.

7. Burton EJ, Barber R, Mukaetova-Ladinska EB, et al. *Medial temporal lobe
   atrophy on MRI differentiates Alzheimer's disease from dementia with Lewy
   bodies and vascular cognitive impairment.* Brain 2009;132(1):195-203.
   doi:10.1093/brain/awn298
   — The classic MTA result, DLB vs AD rather than SAA-stratified. Our visual
   MTA finding (higher in SAA-) sits in this tradition; our CAT12 composite
   contradicts it.

**Where this leaves us.** RBD and hallucinations replicate. Parkinsonism does
not. DaT-SCAN against SAA status appears not to have been reported. The GFAP
result runs against the prevailing AD-co-pathology account and needs replication
before it is claimable. The imaging is an underpowered null and the published
work agrees there is no medial temporal effect to find.
